notes: One command starts the runtime everywhere: `aidog start` (with `status` and `stop`) is now the single entry point on any install. It is idempotent and self-checking — after starting it probes the console's own health endpoint, and when that fails it repairs what it can identify: a session whose process died is recycled, a wedged console process we own is restarted, and a foreign process squatting on the port is reported by pid and never killed. A missing tmux is bootstrapped user-space without admin rights, a missing python3 fails early and honestly, and a health probe counts only our own endpoint so an impostor can never be mistaken for a healthy console. The final gate for append-only release history is now proven: a diverged-installation recovery drill (38 offline assertions) walks the whole backup-first migration — a clone whose history diverged, or shares no ancestry at all, is refused fast-forward with its data untouched; a tar plus git-bundle backup round-trips byte-identically; a fresh clone lands in a sibling directory; configuration, memory, transcripts and the suppression ledger restore into a separate profile with a separate state root; a first reply and the memory filters are verified BEFORE any service path is switched; the original tree stays byte-identical for rollback; and no command anywhere force-pushes, resets or disables fast-forward. The curated memory slots shipped in the repo are now product wording: they point at the owner-managed persona store through configuration instead of naming another project's internal paths and accounts, and the secret-scanning gate stays green. The Windows desktop shell acceptance is recorded from the owner's real-machine test (usable, feature parity with the web console); the macOS checklist still needs a real Mac. Counts: 3036 core, 619 console smoke, 130 setup wizard, 1951 locale keys, 54 modules, ~33.7k lines.
